transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-18
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Dana Cole (Aurora Head of ML), Ravi Singh (Aurora Platform), Marta Lopez (Aurora CTO)
Resources shared: link: /redwood/docs/optimize-batching-kv (deck), cost-model.xlsx (sheet), security-overview.pdf

Summary (auto): Redwood walked through batching and KV cache recommendations, walked cost model for their usage profile, discussed private deployment options (VPC), and agreed on a short pilot to validate latency/cost.

Transcript:
00:00 Marcus (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we got like 55 minutes, we'll run through the Optimize walkthrough, batching and the prefix kv cache model, and then leave time for q's. dana, you mentioned you'll be sharing prompt hist, is that correct?
00:12 Dana (Aurora): yep yep, we'll get that export, um it's a bit messy the traces so i'll ask ravi to clean it up.
00:18 Marcus: perfect. so quick agenda, one: batching overview, two: kv cache prefix behavior, three: cost model with numbers, and four: pilot next steps.
00:27 Sofia (Redwood SE): one note, i'll call out some latency tail behavior — most customers see improvements when moving from naive sync calls to continuous batching and with prefix caching on repeated prompts.
00:39 Ravi (Aurora): can you remind me, prefix cache is same as kv cache? i've seen it called kv, k v, sometimes "kv cache" in your docs.
00:46 Sofia: yep it's the same — K V cache, prefix cache, we sometimes say K V store. it's the token level cached KV for transformer key-value states. apologies for the naming noise, some transcriptions call it K V cache.
00:55 Marta (Aurora): our big question is can you guarantee we won't leak PII in cache? we have regulated data, so need clear purge/TTL.
01:05 Priya (Redwood): short answer is yes — cache eviction policies and scoped caches per-customer are supported, plus optional server-side encryption using your KMS. we'll include that in the security doc.
01:15 Marcus: quick baseline: with your reported distribution — ~70% short prompts (<50 tokens), 20% medium (50-200), 10% long — naive per-request decode cost is high due to repeated prefix computation. batching reduces GPU idle and amortizes kernel launch.
01:30 Sofia: demo slide — if we batch to 8-16 requests with a max latency budget of 120ms, your per-token cost drops ~30% in our model; using KV prefix cache for repeated user contexts can drop it another 25-40% depending on hit rate.
01:48 Dana: what's realistic cache hit rate for a finance app? users often paste similar account summaries so i'd expect decent reuse.
01:56 Sofia: for customer support style where prompts share re-used context, hit rates of 40-60% are common; for transaction summaries maybe 20-35%. we'll model both conservative and optimistic scenarios in the sheet.
02:10 Marcus: important trade-off is memory footprint: larger cache (per-model, per-GPU) increases VM/RAM requirements and slightly increases cost, but reduces per-token compute. in the cost model i show net TCO.
02:24 Ravi: do we need Dedicated / private for that? or hosted can do secure caches?
02:30 Priya: hosted supports scoped cache + encryption but if you need full VPC/on-prem control we can run Private where the control plane is customer-side. both support same runtime features.
02:40 Marta: latency — our SLAs want p95 < 100 ms for brief prompts; is that achievable with batching?
02:46 Sofia: yes, with micro-batching and async streaming we can hit p50/p90 easily; tail (p95/p99) needs careful batching policy rules — e.g., max wait thresholds and overflow fallbacks to smaller batch sizes. we'll show examples.
03:05 Marcus: ok walking through the cost model now — open cost-model.xlsx, sheet 'Aurora-Profile'. baseline: 200 qps, avg prompt 40 tokens, typical response 80 tokens, we modeled hosted vs dedicated vs private.
03:20 Sofia: hosted with moderate batching (batch size expectation 8) + small KV cache (per-GPU 6GB) gives ~0.014 $/1k tokens in our sim; with KV hit 30% effective cost drops to ~0.010 $/1k tokens.
03:36 Dana: that delta is huge if you scale to millions/month. how sensitive is that to avg token length?
03:42 Marcus: quite sensitive — if avg response doubles, cost scales linearly; caching helps most when prompts reuse prefixes. we included a sensitivity tab in the sheet.
03:53 Ravi: concerned about burst traffic peaks — credit card auth flows spike. how does the runtime handle bursts?
04:00 Sofia: two pieces: autoscale pools for Dedicated can absorb steady-state increases, plus burst capacity lanes. plus we support routing policies to fallback to smaller-parameter models for spikes.
04:12 Marta: competitor question — we've seen ads from openai claiming low latencies; how do you compare?
04:18 Marcus: OpenAI is a benchmark but our differentiator is consistent SLOs across private/dedicated/hosted and tooling for unit-economics — Optimize gives explicit cost levers.
04:29 Dana: any case studies with finance customers?
04:32 Priya: we've done pilots with Aurora-like customers, e.g., Novapayments, Aurora Finance (internal pseudonym), and they saw 20-40% TCO reduction after cache + batching tuning.
04:45 Ravi: ok can we dig into microbatch policy examples?
04:49 Sofia: sure — policy A: latency-first, max wait 15 ms, batch up to 6; policy B: cost-first, max wait 80 ms, batch up to 20 with early flush on high-priority requests. show sample config in console screenshot (we shared link).
05:10 Marcus: note that larger batches are more effective on long sequences due to kernel amortization; short prompts benefit less unless you have prefix reuse via KV cache.
05:22 Dana: i want to confirm purge policy — can we set key TTL per-tenant and on-demand purge via API?
05:28 Priya: yes, per-tenant TTL and admin purge API exists; we'll include API endpoint in the security appendix.
05:34 Marcus: quick demo clip — console -> Optimize -> Batching policies (screen described), but audio glitched here (auto transcript says 'screen shnort').
05:46 Sofia: now the numbers: for your 200 qps profile we estimate monthly token volume ~1.2B tokens. baseline hosted cost ~ $16k/month; with 30% KV hit and batching gains it's ~ $11k/month. Dedicated commit pricing would lower unit infra cost but has reserve.
06:10 Ravi: what's the setup time for dedicated?
06:13 Marcus: typical is 4-6 weeks for Dedicated (capacity allocation, infra provisioning) but a hosted pilot can start in days.
06:21 Marta: compliance — do you have SOC2 or ISO?
06:24 Priya: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO27001, and support for customer-managed KMS, SSO/SAML and audit logs. we'll send security pack.
06:34 Dana: fine, pilot scope — what do you propose?
06:37 Marcus: 2-week pilot: 1) baseline run (no batching, no cache), 2) enable batching + small KV cache, 3) run synthetic and real traffic windows and compare latency/cost. we'll use same infra snapshot and perf hooks.
06:50 Ravi: who handles infra for the pilot? we want to run benchmarks from our VPC region.
06:55 Priya: we can run pilot in your VPC with Private control plane or run in our hosted region and give you full telemetry; depends on security needs.
07:05 Marcus: ok let's capture action items.
07:08 Marta: quick q on prompts — can the cache be scoped to user session vs global?
07:12 Sofia: yes scoping options: per-tenant, per-user-session, or ephemeral. commonly choose per-user-session for personalization while preventing cross-user leakage.
07:23 Dana: for the benchmark we will share: sample traces (per-user), target SLOs, and a compliance contact.
07:28 Marcus: noted. we'll share the cost model sheet and SOW.
07:33 Marcus: any final q's?
07:35 Ravi: one last: does cache state persist across restarts? we use rolling updates and need warmup strategy.
07:40 Sofia: KV cache can be backed by persistent store or warm-up warmers; typical approach is snapshotting hot keys and pre-warming on deploy.
07:50 Marcus: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up — sending notes and links.
